findings.message: azdo_rest is a second AzDO REST client. It builds the URL as `https://dev.azure.com/$AZDO_ORG/$AZDO_PROJECT/_apis/...` with the project not URL-encoded and the org not normalised. The existing client in plugins/specclaw-sync/lib/azdo-common.sh (ORG_URL / PROJECT_ENC used by ado_get) does both, so the two copies disagree on the same .env. Fix: reuse the sync client's URL and encoding (or one shared helper), and encode `$AZDO_PROJECT` with `@uri`.
findings.scenario: AZDO_PROJECT="Fleet Platform" (System.TeamProject in the pipeline commonly has spaces), with optin/records working through specclaw-azdo-issue → curl rejects the unencoded URL → doctor always prints `skip pipeline` / `skip service-connections` (rc 2, never clean), status shows `unknown (AzDO unreadable)`, and `--run` builds are always `unknown`, so did-not-run is never inferred and --watch only ends by timeout.

findings.message: The r15 fix moved the PAT Authorization header off curl's argv only in azdo_rest (`-H @-`). The new cmd_whoami in the same diff still passes `-H "Authorization: Basic $(auth_header)"` on argv. It runs on every `optin` (once in fleet_optin and once per change in cmd_optin). Fix: feed the header through stdin or a config file, as azdo_rest does.
findings.scenario: On a shared host or CI agent, run `specclaw-fleet optin 002-a` while another user runs `ps -ef` → the curl process for `_apis/connectionData` shows `Authorization: Basic <base64 :PAT>`, which leaks AZDO_TOKEN (Work Items/Code write).

findings.message: load_fleet_settings returns before trusted_only_settings when the branch has no readable .specclaw/config.yaml. In a pipeline run with FLEET_TRUSTED_CONFIG set, the trusted security settings (node_label, image, namespace, cluster_name, deadline_minutes, ...) are then not applied and defaults are used instead. A missing vault currently stops dispatch, so the impact is limited. Fix: apply the trusted-only settings before the early return whenever FLEET_TRUSTED_CONFIG is set.

An invalid FLEET_AGENT_TIMEOUT falls back to 7200 s with a warning instead of failing the run. 7200 s can exceed the Job's activeDeadlineSeconds when deadline_minutes is lower, so k8s kills the pod before the watchdog delivers. Fix: fail closed with record state=failed exit=bad-agent-timeout.

The trusted-config fail-closed check covers only `git fetch` failing. It has no rows for `git show` failing (trusted branch has no .specclaw/config.yaml) or `git rev-parse` failing (FLEET_TRUSTED_COMMIT empty). Add both rows to the table.

The README lists the security settings as vault, image, namespace, node_label, image_pull_secret and claude_version. FLEET_SECURE_KEYS also includes deadline_minutes and cluster_name, which are likewise trusted-branch-only and stop the run on mismatch. Add them to the doc.
